messages:
rachel: FYI deploy-bot failed pushing canary to ECR during the 09:30 release window.
deploy-bot: [automated] push failed: PutImage Unauthorized - token expired
max: ugh, token expired again? which credential did it use (ci-service-role or ephemeral creds)?
rachel: ci-service-role. I see `ECR: authorization token expired` in the logs. full line:
```
ERROR: PutImage failed: AccessDeniedException: The authorization token has expired
    at com.aws.ecr.Client.putImage(Client.java:...)
```
dani: is the image already created in ECR with a digest? or nothing pushed at all?
rachel: partial. the manifest exists (sha256:6a7f...) but tag `canary/2026-03-20` never landed. Console shows manifest with no tags.
ops-bot: note: images without tags are eligible for garbage collection after 30d. :warning:
jen: hmm that means the current canary tag in prod still points to the previous digest. Do we rollback the canary promotion or retag the new manifest once creds are refreshed?
max: quick option: re-auth and attempt a retag (PutImage with existing manifest). If manifest is intact we can attach tag `canary/2026-03-20` to sha256:6a7f... that was pushed earlier.
rachel: I can refresh credentials and try retagging. But need approvals to touch production tag in the change window.
dani: what's our rollback impact? If we rollback the canary promotion, feature will be delayed but safer.
jen: also we need provenance metadata (build id, git sha) attached. The failed push lost tag but maybe labels exist on manifest. Does ECR store image labels separately?
max: ECR stores imageManifest which includes container config. We typically write provenance as image labels and a `redwood-provenance` manifest entry. If retagging, we must ensure `PutImage` includes the same manifest content so metadata stays.
rachel: plan proposal:
- refresh ci-service-role token (I have perms)
- attempt `PutImage` to add tag to existing manifest (no re-upload)
- verify provenance label `redwood.build` is present; if missing, create a signed provenance object in our artifact-bucket and add a note to the release
- if PutImage fails, rollback canary promotion and open a follow-up for credential rotation
max: commands I'll run (dry-run first):
```
aws ecr get-authorization-token --region us-west-2 | base64 --decode
aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name redwood/runtime --image-ids imageDigest=sha256:6a7f...
aws ecr put-image --repository-name redwood/runtime --image-manifest file://manifest.json --image-tag canary/2026-03-20
```
rachel: please also update the release notes with a note: "canary delayed due to ECR auth token expiry; images retagged once fixed" if we retag.
dani: change window check: still inside 09:30-10:30 window, SLO allows one retry.
ops-bot: change-window: active (approved by eng-leads)
deploy-bot: attempted re-run at 1777005622: Failed: PutImage Unauthorized
rachel: ok I refreshed the role token and retried manually at 1777005650 — PutImage succeeded and tag applied.
max: can verify digest->tag mapping now? I see `canary/2026-03-20 -> sha256:6a7f...` in ECR, good.
jen: provenance check: batch-get-image returned container config with label `redwood.build=20260320-4729` and `git.sha=4f9b2c` — good.
dani: final ops step: add a note to the release PR and increment pinned version in the canary service deployment manifest (helm values) so rollback remains deterministic.
rachel: done: patched helm values in `deploy/canary/values.yaml` to `image.tag: canary/2026-03-20` and pushed commit 9a3b.
jen: thumbs up. please add a short blurb to the release notes and log the incident for postmortem: token TTL is still too short for longer pipelines.
max: filing follow-up: rotate CI token to use STS-assume-role with 1h refresh and add retry + exponential backoff to the deploy-bot. @security please review.
rachel: created ticket INFRA-712: "ECR auth token expiry causing intermittent PutImage failures" and added steps we took. Will coordinate with infra tomorrow.
ops-bot: incident closed: manual remediation succeeded, no rollback required. :white_check_mark:
jen: thanks all — good catch and quick recovery. :thumbsup:
